html:
Ponca (Oklahoma) marks the land of the Ponca Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma, near Ponca City in the north of the state. The Ponca are a Dhegiha Siouan people, close kin of the Omaha, who lived on the Niobrara River in Nebraska. See Ponca for the people as a whole.

In 1877 the United States forced them south to Indian Territory, and many died of disease in the first years. When the chief Standing Bear walked home to bury his son in Nebraska, he was arrested. At his trial in Omaha in 1879 a federal judge ruled that an Indian is a person under the law, with the right to go to court for his freedom. Afterwards some Ponca went back to Nebraska, while the rest stayed in Oklahoma.
